body:
## Bug
After reopening a browser-local draft, the Params input and floating Width control display the original default (60 mm), while the saved source and model-tree parameter display the edited value (85 mm). This can mislead a user about manufacturing dimensions.

## Reproduction
1. In a fresh anonymous browser context open https://app.kernelcad.com/ and wait for Ready, 1 body.
2. The starter script has `const w = param('Width', 60, { unit: 'mm' }); const h = param('Height', 40, { unit: 'mm' }); const t = param('Thickness', 5, { unit: 'mm' }); const base = box(w, h, t); const hole = cylinder(t.add(2), 4).translate(w.divide(2), h.divide(2), -1); return base.subtract(hole);`.
3. Open Params, focus Width, replace `60` with `85`, press Enter. Wait until Saved and Ready.
4. Export STL. Reload https://app.kernelcad.com/ in the same browser context. Wait until Ready.
5. The model tree shows Width 85 and source reads `param('Width', 85, ...)`; the floating Width control and Params input instead show 60. Repeated reload produces the same discrepancy.

Expected: all controls display the persisted value 85, consistent with the script and model. Actual: controls display stale 60. This report does not claim the reopened exported geometry is 60: that was not measured. Initial pre-reload STL had X bounds 0..85, Y 0..40, Z 0..5, 1,024 triangles, 51,284 bytes, SHA256 `0ade11dffb5b80ce19f26db279e5bebbcf5539a099c5503f3ece888667445050`.

## Environment and evidence
2026-11-13, kernelCAD web v0.17.0, work-1 Linux 6.8.0-147, isolated browser context, anonymous local draft. WebGL unavailable in this browser; 3D visualization was not verified. Screenshot of Params after reload: `/home/andrii/ventures/state/q-a/2026-11-13-2345/params-reload.png`; exported STL is alongside it. Browser version should be checked for the harness (host Chrome reports 156.0.8078.79). Not tested with signed-in cloud projects or other browsers. No destructive actions or publication.
title: Reopened local draft shows stale Width in Params and viewport control

body:
## Current status — 12 November 2026

The original hosted physics failure is repaired and verified on build `0.1.0+9e5229a0c0d5@2026-11-12T21:58:50.309Z`. The unchanged original fixture passes; the incompatible-ratio control still fails. Evaluation, mechanism review and physics agree.

This issue remains open for the original fixture's **rendered animation / animation-bake agreement** portion of acceptance criterion 3. Vehicle bearing-support defects remain separate. [Final production evidence](https://github.com/w1ne/kernelCAD-web/issues/1321#issuecomment-6837332578) records exact source hashes, coverage and limits. The original reproducer and acceptance criteria are preserved below.

---

## Reproducer
Published KernelCAD model: https://app.kernelcad.com/p/nMQXpIBa?version=1

The RC buggy uses:
- A 12-tooth involute motor pinion and a 48-tooth rear-axle gear, module 1, 30 mm center distance.
- Revolute mates `motor-input` and `rear-drive-output`.
- `car.coupleMates('rear-drive-output', { source:'motor-input', ratio:-12/48 })` with a `gear-pair` transmission path `['motor-rotor','rear-live-axle']`.
- `motorDeg` parameter and animationView to exercise the gearbox.

## Steps
1. Load the model's source from the project.
2. Run `evaluate_script({code})`. **Actual:** ok=true, diagnostics=[], mechanism='real'.
3. Run `verify({check:'physics',code})`.

## Actual physics-gate failure
- `mechanism.physics-unsupported`: "Could not compute required holding forces at pose 'rear-drive-output:-180': Pose overrides violate the declared coupling to mate 'rear-drive-output'."
- `mechanism.physics-unsupported`: "Native release dynamics could not verify the declared scalar couplings across 502 coordinate checks (500 integration observations)."
- Integration coverage: 500/500.
- Maximum linear residual: 0.00000 mm (tolerance 0.01 mm).
- **Maximum angular residual: 47.6092° at rear-drive-output (tolerance 5°)**.
- Verification fails despite kinematic evaluate passing.

## Expected
- The physics release path preserves the signed -1/4 gear ratio and verifies it through all integration samples.
- The physics test samples independent drive DOFs and propagates driven revolute poses through the authored coupling. It should not independently override the driven rear axle against the source drive constraint.
- Where physics backend cannot represent a coupling, return an explicit unsupported mapping with actionable details rather than a false physics pass.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Add a regression fixture with a 12:48 revolute gear pair and drive input sweep; assert the native physics solver preserves signed 4:1 reduction within the published angular tolerance for all integration steps.
2. Coupling-aware pose generation never issues independent overrides to driven mates.
3. `evaluate_script`, `review_cad`, `verify(check:'physics')`, and animation all agree on drive motion and ratio.
4. Test positive and negative direction, zero crossing, and input angle limits.

This is a **mechanical-simulation blocker**, separate from model-design issues (missing hub bearing shoulders and declared load cases), which must also be resolved before a physically validated RC car claim.
title: Physics verification breaks coupled 12:48 spur-gear drive (47.61° angular residual)

body:
Tracking issue for making the existing kinematics / assembly / physics checks honest, and for the verification-stack plan that should follow.

Goal: every build should be able to run through a proper verification stack so we can verify the quality of our builds. First we fix the checks that already exist and failed (or could not be scored) on real parts. Then, only with an explicit go-ahead, we implement the engine architecture in the companion issue.

## Companion: engine architecture (plan only)

See #1271 for the verification-stack plan (kinematics solver + mobility/rank, collision, MuJoCo loops, mass provenance, clearance/fit, OSS options, Codex scope verdict). **Do not start building new engines from that issue without go-ahead.** The honesty fixes below come first.

## Honesty fixes (file-and-fix order)

Fix order: C, D, A, B, F, then E, G, H.

| Letter | Issue | Check | Real-part finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C | #1263 | `mechanism.rest-interpenetration` | Seeded overlap on clamshell (`dummy` vs `base`, ~48406 mm³) reported as `feature.invalid-args`; `mechanism` field absent |
| D | #1264 | `mechanism.motion-on-fixed-joint` | Planetary cover `translate` driven by an animated param stayed `mechanism=real` |
| A | #1265 | evaluate vs `verify` swept-collision | Shop-release scissor: `evaluate_script` `mechanism=real` (ignore pair `base-frame`/`platform`) while `verify({check:'swept-collision'})` fails at `platform-lift=80` |
| B | #1266 | connector seating | Freight trailer: `mechanism=real` with `assembly.mechanical.connector-not-in-solid` on landing-mount and bogie-mount |
| F | #1268 | `kinematic.pose.out-of-limits` | Animation key 897 on clamshell/scissor/4DOF is clamped by `param()` min/max and never reaches the check; widening bounds makes it fire |
| E | #1267 | SO-100 evaluate / physics | Both timed out at 180 s with no mechanism verdict |
| G | #1269 | closed-loop example | `04-scissor-jack-swept` already broken at rest (`assembly.solver.did-not-converge`, headSlide ~103.92 mm) so loop residual could not be seeded fairly |
| H | #1270 | `verify` static-hold | 4DOF returns `ok=true` with empty diagnostics (no `arm.revolute` actuators) — vacuous pass |

## What already passed on real parts (do not regress)

- `mechanism.orphan-part`: far box on clamshell, shop-release scissor, 4DOF
- `kinematic.pose.out-of-limits` when `param()` bounds are wide enough to admit the out-of-range key (clamshell `lidDeg`/`hinge`, scissor `platformZ`/`platform-lift`, 4DOF `baseYawDeg`/`base-yaw`)
- Clean `evaluate_script` `mechanism=real`: clamshell, shop-release scissor (evaluate only), 4DOF, planetary, GT2
- `verify` swept-collision clean: clamshell, 4DOF
- `verify` physics control: shop-release scissor, 4DOF (not a capacity check)

N/A (no fair seed): `mechanism.disconnect` (far-connector seed rejected), `mechanism.tendon-body-intersect` (no tendons on the seven parts), MuJoCo on true closed loops (exporter is tree-only).

## PR rules

- One concern per PR, against `develop` in this repo.
- Unit test under ~60 s plus real-part evidence: the clean part stays `mechanism=real` (or the documented equivalent), and the seeded defect is caught under the named code.
- Codex consulted on each fix.
- Do not merge without approval.
- No prod config, memory-cap, or billing changes.

Method notes (Codex fairness review, 2026-11-09): score the exact diagnostic code; interpenetration includes mated pairs; do not treat `mechanism.unverified-budget-exceeded` as a collision catch; do not treat MJCF loop-export failure as a gravity failure; animation tracks must drive a real param; static-hold must target `arm.revolute({actuator})` or an explicit N/A — not an empty `ok=true`.
title: Tracking: honest kinematics/physics checks and the verification-stack plan

body:
## Why this issue exists

We need a proper verification stack every build runs through, so kinematics and the other engines can verify the quality of our builds. This issue is an architecture **plan**, not a request to start building new engines.

**Do not start implementing this stack (beyond the honesty fixes in the tracking issue) without an explicit go-ahead.** The broken existing checks come first: #1263, #1264, #1265, #1266, #1267, #1268, #1269, #1270.

Acceptance fixtures for any later work: SO-100, freight trailer, shop-release scissor table, `04-scissor-jack-swept`, planetary gearbox, 4DOF arm, clamshell enclosure, GT2 actuator.

## Codex scope verdict

**FAIR WITH CHANGES** (2026-11-09, `codex exec` on kernelCAD-web, EXIT:0). Codex reviewed source only and did not assign pass/fail to the honesty issues.

Required changes before treating the plan as ready to build:

1. **Kinematics gap is partly stale.** A closed-loop solver already exists: continuation plus a numeric closure-Jacobian rank, Grübler mobility, and typed loop diagnostics (`src/shared/kinematics/loopClosure/analysis.ts`). `checkMechanismTruth` collects solver status and residuals but does not carry the solver’s mobility report and loop diagnostics into its verdict. Integrate and audit that path before adding another DOF gate. Keep describing `mechanism.dof-mismatch` as an overlap-topology proxy (±0.5° overlap-pair-count), not a DOF-rank test.
2. **Define the authoritative verification path.** `evaluate_script` runs mechanism truth by default with physics off; the BREP sweep can be skipped over budget; `mechanism=unverified` does not by itself make `ok` false. Studio recompute deliberately omits the sweep. Define a build/CI profile separately from interactive preview. Report each check as passed / failed / not applicable / unsupported / skipped-with-reason. A required check that is skipped or unsupported must not count as a verified build.
3. **Keep collision claims precise.** Sweep is sampled and single-joint-at-a-time; it cannot certify every multi-joint combination. Prefer authored combined motion paths or explicit pose paths with a bounded sample budget — do not require an exhaustive N^M grid. Rest-contact (`restPoseContact.ts`) does not honor `solvedModel({ ignore })`. Rest penetration is mesh/voxel with BREP candidate/fallback; mate gaps use BREP minimum distance — describe those separately.
4. **Separate physics simulation from actuator capacity.** MuJoCo inverse-dynamics currently checks whether required torques are *finite*, not whether they fit a declared actuator. The drop test skips when every articulated mate is driven. `checkStaticHold` reads `arm.__joints()` and can return an empty successful result when that graph has no joints, so mate-driven `mechanicalJoint` chains need explicit coverage. Do not treat a finite torque as adequate capacity.
5. **Mass provenance must be a shared input.** A first-class per-part mass / CoG / inertia coverage field should record whether values come from declared mass, material density, or a default, and must not let a defaulted mass silently support a strong physical claim. Assembly-path stability uses each part’s mesh CoM against contacts; it does not assess whole-assembly tip-over from aggregate mass.
6. **Scope fit as manufacturing verification.** ISO 286 needs a size feature, a common nominal, and tolerance classes. A global body-to-body gap is not enough. Nominal CAD geometry alone does not prove as-manufactured fit. This belongs in the verification/requirements layer, not as another physics engine.

## What exists vs what is missing

### 1. Kinematics engine

| Exists | Missing / honesty gap |
| --- | --- |
| In-tree mate solver (`solveMates`) with tree FK and a closed-loop continuation solver | Loop residuals surface as `assembly.solver.did-not-converge` / `mechanism.mate-unsatisfied`, but mobility/rank from `loopClosure/analysis.ts` is not part of the mechanism verdict |
| Animation limit check (`kinematic.pose.out-of-limits`) and motion-on-fixed-joint | #1268: `param()` min/max can clamp an out-of-range key so the limit check never sees it. #1264: animated `translate` on a fastened part is missed (`geometryOnlyMotion` only inspects `rotateAxis`) |
| `mechanism.dof-mismatch` | Overlap-pair-count proxy, not Grübler / Jacobian rank |
| `04-scissor-jack-swept` as the real closed-loop cookbook | #1269: already broken at rest (headSlide connectors ~103.92 mm apart) |

Recommendation: **keep and harden the in-tree solver**. Do not replace it with Pinocchio, Drake, or Orocos KDL (wrong job and/or too heavy; KDL is also LGPL). After the honesty fixes: integrate the existing mobility/rank outputs into the verdict and validate them on the named corpus before deciding the solver itself needs more work.

### 2. Collision

| Exists | Missing / honesty gap |
| --- | --- |
| OCCT B-rep interference (`detectInterferences`, `assembly.interference.overlap`) | #1263: rest overlap on `evaluate_script` can abort as `feature.invalid-args` before `mechanism.rest-interpenetration` is written |
| Rest-pose contact (`mechanism.rest-interpenetration`, `mechanism.mate-gap`) and joint-mesh-gap | Rest-contact does not honor `solvedModel({ ignore })` |
| Budgeted single-joint min/mid/max sweep (`mechanism.interpenetration`); `verify({check:'swept-collision'})` | Sweep is not an N^M combination check. Budget 40_000 work units → `mechanism.unverified-budget-exceeded` (warn; must never be scored as a collision catch). #1265: shop-release scissor `ignore: [['base-frame','platform']]` lets `evaluate_script` say `mechanism=real` while verify swept-collision fails on that pair |
| In-tree `TriangleBvh` for mesh workflows | SO-100 evaluate/physics timed out at 180 s (#1267). Optional FCL/Coal broadphase only if a benchmark against `TriangleBvh` + OCCT justifies a new C++ dependency (no maintained upstream WASM drop-in found) |

Recommendation: **OCCT remains the exact B-rep authority**. Mesh/BVH (existing `TriangleBvh`, or FCL/Coal later) is a broadphase only. Prefer authored combined motion paths over an exhaustive multi-joint grid.

### 3. Physics (MuJoCo)

| Exists | Missing / honesty gap |
| --- | --- |
| MuJoCo WASM (Apache-2.0, already in tree) for `mechanism.unstable-under-gravity` (non-finite `mj_inverse` torque) and `mechanism.drops-on-release` (>5° joint or >50 mm body in 0.5 s) | Finite torque ≠ actuator capacity. Capacity lives in `checkStaticHold` (`arm.revolute` actuators / `__joints()`), which can vacuous-pass (#1270) |
| Physics skipped when every articulated mate is driven; passive free joints are informational | Closed-loop graphs are rejected by `assemblyToMjcf` (tree-only) — loops are N/A, not a physics verdict |
| Assembly-path stability support-polygon (projection, not dynamics) | No whole-assembly tip-over from aggregate CoG |

Recommendation: **keep MuJoCo; do not add Bullet or Drake**. After honesty fixes: extend the MJCF emitter with `<equality>` constraints for explicitly supported mate types so closed loops are not silently N/A (soft constraint semantics must stay distinct from exact kinematic closure). Unsupported loop types remain visibly unverified. Wire torque *capacity* through a mate-aware static-hold path, not by pretending `mj_inverse` finiteness is a spec check.

### 4. Mass properties

| Exists | Missing |
| --- | --- |
| Material density presets, inspect mass, BOM mass rows; static-hold uses geometry + density | A first-class evaluate coverage field (mass, CoG, inertia per part) that records provenance (declared / density / default) |
| Per-part mesh CoM in assembly-path stability | Aggregate-CoG support-polygon tip-over that refuses to make a strong claim from defaulted mass |

### 5. Clearance / fit

| Exists | Missing |
| --- | --- |
| `mechanism.mate-gap`, rest contact, `jointClearanceRadius`, process DFM clearances, `assembly.clearance.violated` for declared min gaps | A named fit verify against a declared ISO 286 class on named size features (bore/shaft or parallel faces), with typed error + hint |
| — | Nominal solid interference is not a substitute for a fit table |

ISO 286-1 (size features) and ISO 286-2 (hole/shaft limit deviations); 2010 edition still current after the 2026 review. This is manufacturing verification, not a second engine.

## Open-source engine options (licence / wasm-or-server / speed)

| Option | Licence | Fit | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| In-tree mate solver + `loopClosure/analysis.ts` | already in tree (OCCT-adjacent) | CAD constraints, loop residual, Grübler, Jacobian rank | **Keep.** Integrate mobility/rank into the mechanism verdict. |
| Pinocchio | BSD | Rigid-body FK/ABA; not a CAD constraint solver | **Don’t add** for mate constraints. |
| Drake | BSD-3-Clause | Capable, huge C++ toolchain | **Don’t add** — too heavy for `evaluate_script`. |
| Orocos KDL | LGPL-2.1-or-later | Chain/tree FK/IK, not general mate closure | **Don’t add** (wrong job + LGPL). |
| OCCT B-rep boolean / `BRepExtrema` | existing (LGPL-exception in tree) | Exact rest interference and mate distance | **Keep as source of truth.** |
| In-tree `TriangleBvh` | already in tree | Mesh broadphase | **Benchmark before adding FCL.** |
| FCL / Coal (hpp-fcl) | BSD-3 | Mesh/BVH candidate pairs; C++, no maintained upstream WASM drop-in | **Only if** a measured sweep bottleneck remains after `TriangleBvh` + OCCT. Narrow phase stays OCCT. |
| MuJoCo | Apache-2.0 | Already WASM (~evaluate physics path) | **Keep.** Extend equality-constraint emission for supported loops. |
| Bullet | zlib | Second physics engine | **Don’t add.** |

## Proposed build order (after the honesty fixes, and only with go-ahead)

1. Define the authoritative build profile, per-check coverage, and the rule that a required skipped/unsupported check is not a verified build.
2. Integrate and audit the existing loop mobility/rank outputs and typed diagnostics; validate on the named corpus before deciding the solver needs more work.
3. Verify authored combined motion paths for collision, using bounded sampling and OCCT as the B-rep authority. Make `ignore` vs sweep vs rest-contact consistent and explicit.
4. Add shared mass-property provenance and extend gravity-hold *capacity* checks to mate-driven actuator chains.
5. Extend MJCF loop support for explicitly supported mate types; unsupported cases stay visibly unverified.
6. Add aggregate-CoG support-polygon stability for assembled loads.
7. Add named ISO-fit verification against declared size features and tolerance classes.
8. Revisit FCL/Coal only if measured sweep performance still justifies it.

## Out of scope until go-ahead

- Replacing the mate solver
- Adding Pinocchio, Drake, Orocos KDL, Bullet, or a second collision kernel
- Treating budget-skip / loop-export-failure / finite `mj_inverse` torque as a physics catch
title: Verification-stack architecture: kinematics, collision, physics, mass, and fit engines

## Current verified baseline (2026-11-09)
- Hosted `https://mcp.kernelcad.com/mcp` accepts MCP initialize with HTTP 200 and reports tools.
- Official MCP Registry currently lists `com.kernelcad/kernelcad` **latest version 0.17.1** (search API: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=kernelcad&limit=100).
- The current public repository `server.json` at `origin/develop` declares **0.17.4**; `/tmp/mcp-publisher validate` passed against the production registry.
- Site already has indexable content, robots, sitemap, and `llms.txt`. New canonical CAD MCP landing is in private marketing PR https://github.com/w1ne/kernelCAD-server/pull/619.
- ChatGPT app deep link is present on the homepage, but public directory discoverability was not verified through app search; do not confuse the deep link with public approval.
- Claude custom connector works as an integration path; public directory review/approval has not been verified.

## Actions
1. Publish `com.kernelcad/kernelcad` **0.17.4** to official registry using the existing domain-controlled HTTP/DNS identity. Preserve or deliberately rotate the existing proof key at `https://kernelcad.com/.well-known/mcp-registry-auth`—do not publish another registry identity or expose private keys in issues or CI logs.
2. Verify Registry API reports 0.17.4 as `isLatest=true`, with correct endpoint and description.
3. In the authorized OpenAI Developer Platform account, verify KernelCAD's ChatGPT directory submission and publication status; if not public, submit current plugin package with tested MCP flows, truthful metadata, privacy/terms, and screenshots. Do not call it published until confirmed.
4. In the authorized Claude developer portal, verify or submit the remote connector/plugin for directory review, then record public listing URL and review status.
5. Record baseline impressions/CTR/position from actual Google Search Console or Bing Webmaster Tools, with locale and date; avoid asserting rank #1 from generic search snippets.

## Acceptance
- 0.17.4 is latest in official MCP Registry.
- Public ChatGPT and Claude statuses are explicitly verified and URLs stored (or blockers recorded).
- An unauthenticated user can discover the product landing page, and an authorized user can connect and complete the mechanical CAD smoke task. No unsupported claims about rankings.

### Portal blockers observed
- OpenAI Platform on the connected work-1 browser reached a sign-in screen, not an authenticated developer dashboard.
- Claude directory manage reached the security challenge and a sign-in page, not an authenticated submission dashboard.
title: Distribution: update official MCP Registry and confirm public ChatGPT / Claude listings

body:
Hi - I run Dominion Observatory (https://dominionobservatory.com), which checks MCP tool manifests for changes. An agent builds against the tool description and input schema it last read. If either changes silently, its calls start failing or return something different, and it has no way to notice.

I read your public endpoint `https://mcp.kernelcad.com/mcp` today with an unauthenticated JSON `tools/list` request (standard MCP initialize handshake, no credentials):
- 71 tools
- SHA-256 of the tools array (sorted keys, compact JSON): `e9fb4dd7d5cfbc856fc4617087a58982fbbd660e2b90ee99f3e99bf02aed5c8b`
- first tools: review_paint_peek_latest, open_in_studio, get_project
- read at 2026-10-28T06:04Z

I kept this snapshot private. If a signed baseline JSON would be useful - an independent record your users can check future manifests against, whatever your release process - or a fresh comparison after your next release, reply here or email info@dominionobservatory.com. Free, no strings. I only listed the tools; I did not call them, and this is not a vulnerability report or a claim about access to tool execution.

If this isn't useful or issues are the wrong place, say so and I'll leave it there.

Dinesh, Dominion Observatory
title: Free private tools/list baseline for your agent-facing endpoint
